title: Perfect complexes are dualizable
statement: Let $p$ and $\ell$ be distinct primes, let $a,n\geq1$ be integers, put $q=p^a$, let $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ and $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, and let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be a finite extension with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$. Put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ and choose $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$. Fix a six-functor datum [def-sf-datum] on finite-type $k$-schemes and separated finite-type morphisms, and let $X$ be a scheme in that datum. Use its category $D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ and the coefficient unit $\Lambda_X$, derived tensor and derived internal Hom of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Thus the integral unit is the completed coefficient sheaf and the field stages use scalar localization and the common finite-stage category, respectively. Let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ be quasi-isomorphic, locally on the coefficient site of $X$, to a bounded complex of finite projective $\Lambda_X$-modules: at every coefficient stage the local terms are actual direct summands of finite sums of the coefficient unit, with the localized and common-stage interpretations of [def-weil-site-perfect-complex]. Then $K^\vee=R\mathcal Hom_X(K,\Lambda_X)$ is perfect on the coefficient site of $X$ in that same sense, and the evaluation $K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}K^\vee\to\Lambda_X$ is defined.

proof.text: First treat finite and integral coefficients. In the finite case put $R=(A_{E,n})_X$; in the integral case put $R=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}$. Internal Hom at the integral stage is the ambient ringed-site derived internal Hom, as specified in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]; no comparison of completed and uncompleted tensor is needed to compute this dual. For an arbitrary object of the small coefficient site choose a cover on whose members $K$ has a bounded representative $P^\bullet$, zero outside $[a,b]$, with finite-projective terms, as in [def-weil-site-perfect-complex]. Restriction is exact by [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], and [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction] identifies $(K^\vee)|_U$ with $R\mathcal Hom_{R|_U}(K|_U,R|_U)$. We can therefore calculate on each such slice. Refine its cover, for the finitely many nonzero terms, so that each $P^r$ has a displayed retraction $P^r\xrightarrow{i_r}R^{\oplus m_r}\xrightarrow{p_r}P^r$, $p_ri_r=1$. These are separate degreewise retractions, not a splitting of $P$ as a complex.

source.place: Tags 08JB (lemma-restriction-RHom-to-U), 08JJ (lemma-dual-perfect-complex), locality paragraph; coefficient conventions in the cited operations definition

proof.text: For one of these terms $E=P^r$, precomposition gives maps $\mathcal Hom(E,R)\xrightarrow{\mathcal Hom(p_r,R)}\mathcal Hom(R^{\oplus m_r},R)\xrightarrow{\mathcal Hom(i_r,R)}\mathcal Hom(E,R)$ whose composite is $1$. Evaluation on the standard basis identifies the middle sheaf with $R^{\oplus m_r}$. Thus $E^\vee$ is finite projective. For every module sheaf $B$, precomposition with $p_r$ and $i_r$ gives natural maps $\mathcal Hom(E,B)\to B^{\oplus m_r}\to\mathcal Hom(E,B)$ with composite $1$. Thus $\mathcal Hom(E,-)$ is a retract, as an additive functor, of the finite-sum functor $(-)^{\oplus m_r}$. This is exact: a short exact sequence for the finite-sum functor splits into the two sequences belonging to the idempotent and its complement, and kernels and images split into the same summands. This holds on every slice, hence for sheaves. These arguments use only composition and finite tuples; $m_r=0$ gives the zero functor. The formula for sheaf Hom and its restriction is the one in [def-pur-hom-complex] and [def-pur-derived-internal-hom].

source.place: Tag 08JJ, finite-free/direct-summand calculation; Tag 08JI (lemma-Rhom-complex-of-direct-summands-finite-free), exactness of term Hom

proof.text:
Take a K-injective resolution $R[0]\to I$ provided in [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. The bounded complex $P$ satisfies the exact-term hypothesis of [lem-pc-bounded-exact-term-hom-quasi-iso] by step 2. That lemma applied to $R[0]\to I$ gives a quasi-isomorphism $D=\mathcal Hom^\bullet_R(P,R[0])\to\mathcal Hom^\bullet_R(P,I)$. The latter represents $R\mathcal Hom_R(P,R)$ by the definition of derived internal Hom, so $D$ represents $(K^\vee)|_U$. By [def-pur-hom-complex] its terms and differential are
$$D^j=\mathcal Hom_R(P^{-j},R),\qquad d_D^j(\phi)=(-1)^{j+1}\phi\circ d_P^{-j-1}.$$
There is only one possibly nonzero factor in each degree of this Hom complex; thus no infinite-product interchange occurs. The complex $D$ is zero outside $[-b,-a]$ and its terms are finite projective by step 2. The dual therefore has the local models required by [def-weil-site-perfect-complex], at finite and integral coefficients. No bound uniform over all covering objects has been imposed.

source.place: Tag 08JJ (lemma-dual-perfect-complex), strictly perfect calculation; Tag 08JI (lemma-Rhom-complex-of-direct-summands-finite-free); Tag 08J7, definition of derived internal Hom

proof.text: Now let $\Lambda=E$. Use the actual local finite-projective models in the scalar-localized category of [def-weil-site-perfect-complex], rather than assume that an arbitrary rational splitting lifts integrally. Slice restriction of internal Hom is obtained by restricting the integral internal-Hom construction and then extending its action on morphisms linearly, exactly as in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. The ringed-site restriction and exactness theorem [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction] and the exact scalar localization [lem-weil-linear-scalar-localization-triangulated] consequently give slice restriction and exactness of this rational Hom. Write $H(-)=R\mathcal Hom(-,E_U)$ on such a slice. For the integral unit $R_U$, the map $R_U[0]\to I$ in [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] gives $R\mathcal Hom_{R_U}(R_U,R_U)\cong R_U$, since $\mathcal Hom_{R_U}(R_U,-)$ is the identity functor. Rationalizing this particular isomorphism identifies $H(E_U)$ with $E_U$. This calculation takes place on the ringed slice and requires no scheme-level adjunction on $U$. For a displayed summand $F\xrightarrow{i}E_U^{\oplus m}\xrightarrow{p}F$, $pi=1$, the maps $H(p)$ and $H(i)$ split $H(F)$ off $E_U^{\oplus m}$, since $H(i)H(p)=H(pi)=1$. Additivity of these Hom operations follows directly from their linear action on maps in the operations definition. Thus the rational dual of every term is again a finite-projective term, with its actual splitting in the localized category.

source.place: Tag 08JJ, finite-free/direct-summand argument, extended by the specified scalar localization; current blueprint prop-sf-dualizable.proof.md, local dual model

proof.text: Keep the rational local model $P$ and write $R=R_U$. Fix $j:R[0]\to I$ as in [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. By [def-weil-site-perfect-complex], $P$ is an actual bounded cochain model, zero outside $[a,b]$, whose degree-zero terms become finite-free summands after localization. Apply [lem-sf-rational-term-hom-comparison] with $A=\mathcal O_E$, $t=\varpi_E$ and the completed coefficient sheaf $R$. For each $F=P^r$, the specified chain map $c_F:\mathcal Hom_R(F,R)[0]\to\mathcal Hom_R^\bullet(F[0],I)$ becomes an isomorphism after localization, and its source is a summand of a finite sum of the rational unit. The splittings here are rational; none is assumed to lift integrally.

source.place: Tag 08JI (lemma-Rhom-complex-of-direct-summands-finite-free), finite-free/retract comparison extended to scalar-localized module terms; current blueprint prop-sf-dualizable.proof.md, middle sentence

proof.text: Form the actual module complex $D=\mathcal Hom_R^\bullet(P,R[0])$ using [def-pur-hom-complex]. Its terms are $D^j=\mathcal Hom_R(P^{-j},R)$ and its differential is $d_D^j(\phi)=(-1)^{j+1}\phi\circ d_P^{-j-1}$. Thus $D$ vanishes outside $[-b,-a]$ and its differential squares to zero by the defining Hom formula. Step 5 supplies a rational finite-free summand presentation of each degree-zero module term. These are precisely the allowed rational terms of [def-weil-site-perfect-complex]. Define the comparison $c_P:\mathcal Hom_R^\bullet(P,R[0])\to\mathcal Hom_R^\bullet(P,I)$ by postcomposition with $j$. It is a chain map by the functoriality in [def-pur-hom-complex].

source.place: Tag 08JI (lemma-Rhom-complex-of-direct-summands-finite-free), finite-free/retract comparison extended to scalar-localized module terms; current blueprint prop-sf-dualizable.proof.md, middle sentence

proof.text: Write $P_{\ge r}$ for the stupid tail, equal to $P$ in degrees at least $r$ and zero below. The sequence $0\to P_{\ge r+1}\to P_{\ge r}\to P^r[-r]\to0$ is split degree by degree. Apply [lem-pc-stupid-tail-hom-short-exact] to the source $P_{\ge r}$, its lowest degree $r$, and the target map $j:R[0]\to I$. It gives the three maps $c_{P^r[-r]}$, $c_{P_{\ge r}}$, $c_{P_{\ge r+1}}$ as a morphism of two short exact sequences of Hom complexes. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] to this morphism. Its naturality clause includes the connecting square, so these three comparisons form a morphism of distinguished triangles. No compatibility is inferred merely from agreement of the objects.

source.place: Tag 08JC (lemma-RHom-triangulated), termwise split Hom sequence; Tag 0152 (lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor), naturality including connecting maps

proof.text: Apply the exact scalar-localization functor of [lem-weil-linear-scalar-localization-triangulated] to the triangle morphism in step 7. The target Hom complex $\mathcal Hom_R^\bullet(P_{\ge r},I)$ represents $H(P_{\ge r})$ by [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. For the quotient, the defining Hom formula identifies $c_{P^r[-r]}$ with $c_{P^r}[r]$: the source is concentrated in degree $-r$, and the target differential is $d_I$ on maps from that single degree. The shift isomorphism multiplies a degree-$q$ component by $(-1)^{rq}$ on both sides, which commutes with postcomposition by $j$. Thus the localized quotient comparison is the shift of the isomorphism in step 5.

source.place: Tag 08J7, Hom-complex construction; Tag 08JC, triangle compatibility; scalar-localization conventions of the operations definition

proof.text: The tail $P_{\ge b+1}$ is zero, so its comparison is an isomorphism. Induct downward on $r$ from $b$ to $a$, with inductive claim that the localized map $c_{P_{\ge r}}$ is invertible. In the triangle morphism of steps 7–8, the quotient comparison is invertible by step 5 and its shift calculation, and the next-tail comparison is invertible by the induction hypothesis. [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] makes the middle comparison invertible. At $r=a$ this proves that $D$ represents the rational internal dual of $P$, hence of $K|_U$. Since step 6 gives its bounded finite-projective module terms, [def-weil-site-perfect-complex] gives rational site-perfectness. This uses finitely many tails and no infinite totalization or local-vanishing test in a raw scalar localization.

source.place: Tag 08JJ, bounded dual model; finite stupid-tail induction expanding the blueprint middle sentence

proof.text: For $\Lambda=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, [def-weil-site-perfect-complex] gives a site-perfect representative of $K$ over a finite coefficient field. By [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] and [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], its internal dual in the common-stage category is represented, over that same field (or a finite common extension), by its rational internal dual. Steps 4--9 give local bounded finite-projective models for this rational dual. If a further finite field is chosen, the exact scalar-extension functor of [lem-weil-scalar-extension-exact-triangulated] preserves the finite cone construction; it also preserves finite sums and the splitting equation $pi=1$. The internal-Hom and unit comparisons of [lem-fix-operation-reduction] identify this extended dual with the common-stage dual. These models therefore establish the asserted perfectness at the algebraically closed stage too.

source.place: Local dual model, with the coefficient operations and common finite-stage conventions explicitly expanded

proof.text:
Finally use the specified adjunction $K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}-\dashv R\mathcal Hom_X(K,-)$ in [sk-def-sf-operations], clause (i). Its counit at the coefficient unit is an actual morphism
$$K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}R\mathcal Hom_X(K,\Lambda_X)\longrightarrow\Lambda_X.$$
Equivalently it is the transpose of the identity of $K^\vee$. This defines the evaluation in the statement at each coefficient stage, using that stage's tensor and unit. This last construction does not require a choice of the local models or a gluing of their evaluations.

source.place: Final sentence: evaluation is the counit of tensor–internal-Hom adjunction
